chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

The ill-gotten gain (al-suh't) is the price of the deceased (animal), and the price of the dog, and the price of wine, and the dowry of the prostitute, and the bribe in judgment, and the payment of the soothsayer.
ai.seo_question: What constitutes ill-gotten gain (suh't) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides a concise taxonomy of 'al-suh't' by linking monetary value directly to the intrinsic prohibition of the underlying commodity or service, such as wine and dogs. This definition extends beyond mere impurity to include the corruption of justice (bribery) and the exploitation of spiritual ignorance (soothsaying), establishing a comprehensive framework for financial ethics in Shia jurisprudence. It underscores that the illegality stems from the source's inherent status rather than just the transaction method.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The ill-gotten gain is the price of the deceased, and price of the dog, and the price of the wine, and a dowry of the prostitute, and the bribe regarding the judgement, and the payment of the soothsayer’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Receiving payment for carcasses, dogs, wine, indecent (sexual) relation and a bribe to issue a judgment and payment for foretelling is Suht (unlawful and filthy).”’
